review.note: Applies the 2026-10-19 review and #216. The old default had no dwell (cycloidal 180° up, 180° down), so it read as an eccentric. The default is now rise 120°, dwell 60°, return 120°, dwell 60°, h 22, cycloidal on both flanks: the cam reads as the displacement diagram wrapped round the base circle. The outline is the roller's envelope on the pitch curve, so the lift is exactly the law. The pressure angle peaks at 23.6° (the review's about 23°). Output character corrected from Harmonic to Dwell. The bridge off the cam face is hardware. Rebuild R5 (#216): built on v3 from this record. The cam's outline is made from the cam-contact joint's own law (the roller's envelope), so the build and the kinematics cannot differ. The lift, base-radius and motion-law controls are not offered: the cam is built at build time and a control cannot reshape it (as the pilots' tooth-count controls); the record keeps the design values. The stem is guided off the cam's sweep (shape.guide), so no rail or bridge lies over the cam; the cam is overhung on its live shaft in a housing under the base.

claims.text: rises 22 mm over 120° of cam turn
dwells at the top for 60°, returns over 120° and dwells at the bottom for 60°

edit.explain.motion: As the cam turns, the roller rides its edge and the follower rises and falls along its guide. In this default the follower rises 22 mm over 120° of cam turn, dwells at the top for 60°, returns over 120° and dwells at the bottom for 60°, with the cycloidal law on the rise and the return. The cam is the displacement diagram wrapped round its base circle, so any timing can be drawn into the outline.
edit.explain.forces: The cam can only push along the contact normal through the roller centre. The pressure angle between that normal and the follower path decides how much of the push goes sideways into the guide. Here it peaks at 23.6°, part way up the rise and part way down the return; keep it under about 30°. A spring or gravity must hold the follower on the cam.
edit.ratio.typical: stroke = rise h (22 mm by default) per cam turn, with 60° dwells at the top and the bottom
edit.build.defining_relations: Cycloidal law s = h(f - sin(2 pi f)/(2 pi)), f = theta/beta, on the 120° rise and the 120° return, with 60° dwells at the top and the bottom. The roller centre runs on the pitch curve r = rb + rr + s(theta); the cam outline is the roller's envelope (the pitch curve offset inward by rr), so the lift follows the law exactly. Pressure angle phi = atan(s'/(rb + rr + s)) for an in-line follower: 23.6° at most with the defaults (keep phi < 30°). The pitch curve is convex everywhere, its least radius of curvature 37.5 mm, well above rr, so the outline has no undercut.
edit.build.range: cam 360° continuous; follower lift 0 to 22 mm: rise 120°, dwell 60°, return 120°, dwell 60°
edit.build.notes: The outline is the envelope of the roller, so the roller centre follows the law exactly. The pressure-angle label turns red past 30°. Roller spin is passive. The cam turns counter-clockwise in plan.
edit.topology.notes: ground, cam, follower stem, roller; cam contact is the higher pair; counted mobility 2, because the roller's spin about its pin is a passive extra freedom

review.note: Applies the 2026-10-19 review and #216. Rebuilt in its true orientation and seen in front elevation: camshaft on top, the follower vertical below it, the opening finger pressing the stem's end down and the forked closing bell crank lifting the collar. The law is now rise 90°, return 90°, closed 180°, h 12 (was 60°, 60° and 10), so half the frames show it open. The lobes read as distinct: the opening lobe grows from 18 to 26.4 mm, the closing lobe shrinks from 31.9 to 22.4 mm over the same angles. The loaded rocker is the view highlight: opening rocker from 0° to 45° and from 135° to 180°, closing rocker from 45° to 135°. Keeping supports off the lobes and shoes is hardware work, not record data.

views.note: the rocker that carries the follower: the opening rocker while it accelerates down or brakes on the way up, the closing rocker while it brakes on the way down or accelerates up

edit.ratio.typical: lift 12 mm per cam turn: rise 90°, return 90°, closed 180°
edit.build.ground: head plate standing upright: camshaft O on top, rocker pivots Q1 and Q2 beside and below it, follower guide vertical below
edit.build.defining_relations: Lift y = s(theta), cycloidal, rise 90°, return 90°, closed 180°, h 12. Opening rocker: a finger pivoted at Q1, shoe 56 mm and nose 80 mm from the pivot, so psi1 = asin(y/80) (8.6° at full lift); its lobe is the envelope of the Ø16 shoe, radius 18 mm closed to 26.4 mm at full lift. Closing rocker: a bell crank pivoted at Q2, fork arm 50 mm level to the collar, cam arm 39.7 mm at 107.7° to it, on the tangent to the shoe circle; psi2 = asin(y/50) (13.9° at full lift); its lobe is the envelope of its shoe offset by the 0.1 mm lash, radius 31.9 mm closed to 22.4 mm at full lift. Both lobes are cut from the same law, so at every angle both shoes touch (conjugate): the opening lobe grows where the closing lobe shrinks. Pressure angles at most 23.1° (opening) and 27.7° (closing).
edit.build.range: camshaft 360° continuous; follower 0 to 12 mm lift in 180° of cam, closed for 180°
edit.build.notes: Seen in front elevation. Highlight the rocker currently carrying the follower: the opening rocker from 0° to 45° and from 135° to 180° of cam, the closing rocker from 45° to 135°. Keep the lash visible but tiny. The two lobes lie side by side on the shaft and overlap in this view: tell them apart by pattern and stacking.
edit.topology.notes: ground, camshaft (opening and closing lobes), opening rocker, closing rocker, follower; cam-rocker and rocker-follower contacts; overconstrained on purpose (conjugate cams): counted mobility 0, the four contacts hold one motion

review.note: New review against the record (#216, unbuilt). The record's 20° dwells (160° rise, 160° return) would go by in a blink, and its 29.8° peak pressure angle sat on the 30° limit. Decided: rise 120°, dwell 60°, return 120°, dwell 60°, the cam family's timing, so the slide visibly stops at each end; stroke 30 mm on a 60 mm pitch radius, so the pressure angle peaks at 25.5°. Default view is front elevation with the roller on the near side, where the groove's slope under the roller is the pressure angle at true size. The groove is a boolean on the cylinder (a build kit).

claims.text: here Rp is 60 mm and phi peaks at 25.5°

edit.explain.motion: A groove cut around the drum surface wanders along the axis. A roller sitting in the groove is carried with it, so the follower slide moves parallel to the drum axis as the drum turns. The default groove rises 30 mm over 120°, dwells 60°, returns over 120° and dwells 60°.
edit.explain.forces: Groove walls push both ways, so no return spring is needed. The pressure angle is set by groove slope: tan(phi) = s'/Rp, where Rp is the pitch radius; a larger drum gives a gentler slope and lower side load. In this default, here Rp is 60 mm and phi peaks at 25.5°.
edit.ratio.typical: stroke = groove axial travel (30 mm by default) per drum turn
edit.build.defining_relations: z = s(theta), cycloidal s = h(f - sin(2 pi f)/(2 pi)) on a 120° rise and a 120° return, 60° dwells at each end. Groove slope ds/dx with x = Rp theta; pressure angle phi = atan(s'/Rp); max s' = 2h/beta = 28.6 mm/rad at Rp 60 gives phi max 25.5°.
edit.build.range: drum 360° continuous; slide 0 to 30 mm and back per turn, dwelling 60° at each end
edit.build.notes: Drum axis horizontal, roller on the near side in front elevation. The groove is a boolean: the roller's sweep along the pitch curve, cut from the cylinder, 0.1 mm wider than the roller. Shift drums use stepped dwell grooves instead.
edit.topology.notes: ground, drum, follower slide, roller; roller in groove is a form-closed cam contact; counted mobility 2, because the roller's spin about its pin is a passive extra freedom

review.note: New review against the record (#216, unbuilt). The proportions teach: 45° steps are large, the 240° dwell is two thirds of the turn, so two of six frames move and four stand still, and the modified sine law gives a smooth start and stop (Cv 1.76, Ca 5.53; peak turret speed 0.66 times the camshaft's). The principle is where the rib changes from straight (locking two rollers) to twisted (driving them), so a detail view of the rib between the two rollers is declared and a roller is traced with equal-time ticks. Both axes are drawn: perpendicular and skew, 100 mm apart. Isometric default view shows the cam side-on and the turret in one picture.

claims.text: peak turret speed 0.66 times the camshaft's

edit.build.notes: Camshaft axis horizontal, turret axis vertical, perpendicular and skew at the centre distance. Two adjacent rollers straddle the rib in dwell; during index one roller leaves while the next enters. The rollers turn on their studs (passive, not modelled).
edit.topology.notes: ground, globoidal cam shaft, turret with radial rollers; two rollers in contact with the rib at all times (preloaded), so the pair is overconstrained on purpose: counted mobility 0, the two contacts hold one motion
